marta: FYI bringing up mosaic-13B-v2 from HF — our `hf-to-redwood` convert job failed on the config.json step. Main incompatibilities I see: `rope_scaling`, `sliding_window`, `num_key_value_heads` != `num_attention_heads`, and `max_position_embeddings` way larger than our runtime expects. Anyone run into this?

jon: yup. rope_scaling is an HF extension we mostly ignore, but `sliding_window` changes how the KV cache is laid out (we assume fixed offsets). That one broke our loader.

ryan: can you paste the config snippet?

marta: here's the relevant part:
```json
{
  "max_position_embeddings": 32768,
  "rope_scaling": {"type":"linear", "factor":0.5},
  "sliding_window": true,
  "num_key_value_heads": 64,
  "num_attention_heads": 32
}
```

jon: oof — `num_key_value_heads` > `num_attention_heads` is a pretty common HF oddity for models with grouped kv heads. Our runtime assumes kv heads == attention heads.

liz: quick options: 1) rewrite the loader to remap kv->attn by splitting/replicating heads, 2) derive kv projection shape from the weight tensors instead of config.json, or 3) fallback to a compatibility shim that clamps `num_key_value_heads` to `num_attention_heads` and emits a warning. Option 2 is safest if weights are canonical.

marta: weights do show kv_proj shape (512, 4096) which implies head grouping, but the HF config lies. I tried option 3 locally and it allowed conversion, but then inference segfaulted when `sliding_window=true` because our KV indexing code still expects contiguous cache slices.

jon: sliding_window basically implements a circular KV buffer with windowed attention — we don't support that at runtime yet. Best pragmatic path: disable sliding_window in converted config and emulate by chunked prefix caching at the Redwood layer. Works for most chat workloads.

marta: I also ran quantization experiments after clamping max_position_embeddings to 16384 and forcing `num_key_value_heads`=32. 4-bit quant (awq) looked ok, but I saw a small quality regression (~3% perplexity up) on our convo eval set when sliding_window is disabled.

ryan: 3% isn't great but maybe acceptable depending on latency/cost wins. Did you run the prompt-level refresh evals? Any hallucination/regression hits?

marta: ran ~200 prompts from our regression suite. A few template-sensitive cases degraded — mostly long-turn coherence. Suspect rope_scaling emulation is needed for very long contexts; clamping positions + simple linear rope scaling emulation reduced the gap.

liz: note: rope_scaling in HF can be `linear` or `dynamic`. For emulation we apply a scaled rotary embedding factor during KV build: multiply sin/cos positions by factor. It's imperfect but helped in your run?

marta: yes, applying a conservative factor (0.75) to the embeddings reduced the perplexity delta to ~1% and fixed several coherence failures.

jon: please open an issue with reproduction steps + the failing convo ids so we can triage. Also add a conversion test that detects `num_key_value_heads` mismatch and tries weight-shape-based inference before assuming config is authoritative.

marta: filing one now. PR incoming for two things: (A) loader fallback to infer kv heads from weight shapes, (B) conversion flag `--disable-sliding-window` that rewrites config and annotates the converted model with notes about the emulation.

convert-bot: convert-job-1227 failed — reason: incompatible num_key_value_heads (64 vs 32). See job logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/convert/1227/logs

ryan: thanks — once the PR lands, can we run a canary with quant 4-bit and keep the original HF artifact in our staging bucket for quick A/B?

liz: yes — canary + perf profile. Also add evals for long-turn coherence and streaming latency.

marta: noted. I'll attach the quant experiment logs and eval diffs to the issue. TL;DR: workflow that worked for mosaic-13B-v2 = clamp max_position_embeddings to 16384, infer kv heads from weights, disable sliding_window + emulate with prefix chunks, emulate rope_scaling via scaled rotary factors. Leaves a small quality delta but enables 4-bit quant and inference on our runtime.

jon: sounds good. we should doc this pattern in the HF->Redwood onboarding checklist (special tokens, chat templates, tokenizer quirks, AND these config.json gotchas).

marta: Agreed — adding a short howto to the onboarding repo after the PR. :+1:

liz: nice work — hope we can automate more of this so future bring-ups are smoother. :rocket:
